pre.question: A webpage is difficult to read, but other apps look fine. Which adjustment best fits?
pre.why: Browser zoom changes webpage size. Choose the control that matches the problem.

pre.question: A partner needs your availability, but not appointment details. Which calendar share fits?
pre.why: Free/busy can support scheduling without disclosing event details. Verify the service’s options.

pre.question: Autocorrect changes a person’s name in your message. What should you do?
options: Review and correct the name before sending
Assume the suggestion is always correct
pre.why: Automation can save time but needs review, especially for names, addresses and meaning.

pre.question: Before printing 20 copies, what is the most useful check?
options: Confirm the printer and preview one test page
pre.why: Verify the destination and output before sending a large print job.

pre.question: You manage personal and volunteer accounts. What is a sensible practice?
options: Post every message from whichever account opens
Check the active account and use separate credentials
pre.why: Check the identity and audience. Keep credentials distinct and use appropriate account protections.

pre.question: A nonurgent work message is ready late at night. What should guide when you send it?
options: Recipient expectations, urgency and working hours
How many emojis are in it
pre.why: Timing and a clear response expectation help the recipient respond appropriately.

pre.question: Which wording best respects different levels of experience?
options: Here are the steps; tell me where more detail would help.
Everyone your age struggles with this.
This is obvious, so do not ask questions.
pre.why: Inclusive communication explains context and avoids assumptions about age, culture or ability.

pre.question: An app feature has changed. What is a useful learning response?
options: Assume all old instructions still apply
Give up without identifying the task
Check official help for your version and try the steps
pre.why: Version-specific help and a precise question support independent learning.

pre.question: You need a nearby library computer class. Which search is most useful?
options: Library computer class plus your town
pre.why: Search terms should identify the service and location needed for the task.

pre.question: A post claims a community service is available everywhere. How should you check it?
options: Trust it because it is first in search
Count how many colors the page uses
pre.why: Responsible sources and corroborating evidence matter more than ranking or appearance.

pre.question: An accurate page describes a service in another state. Why might it be unsuitable?
options: It may not be relevant to your local need
pre.why: Accuracy, currency and relevance are separate questions.

pre.question: Before submitting an online form, what should you check?
options: Whether you can enter extra private details
Who collects the data, required fields and the confirmation
pre.why: Understand the collection purpose, provide only needed information, and check the result.

pre.question: Which feature creates a document structure useful to readers and assistive technology?
pre.why: Real heading styles provide structure; visual bolding alone does not.

pre.question: B2, B3 and B4 contain costs. Which formula totals all three?
pre.why: A colon marks an inclusive cell range. Verify the formula by changing one input.

pre.question: You find an image online for a handout. What should you do before reusing it?
options: Check permission or license and provide required credit
Assume search results are free to reuse
pre.why: Find the actual reuse permission and follow its conditions.

pre.question: A partner needs to revise your paragraphs. Which format best fits?
options: An editable document with appropriate access
Only a photograph of the page
An audio recording with no text
pre.why: Choose the format and access that support the recipient’s task. PDF is often useful for finished layout.

pre.question: Which email subject best supports a clear request?
pre.why: A specific subject tells the recipient what the message concerns.

pre.question: What does Bcc do in an email?
options: Hides Bcc recipient addresses from other recipients
pre.why: Bcc hides recipient addresses; it does not encrypt content or prevent forwarding.

pre.question: Before starting a free app trial, what should you inspect?
options: Renewal price, timing and cancellation terms
pre.why: Free trials can become recurring subscriptions. Review the terms and total cost.

pre.question: A free game offers an in-app upgrade. What should you remember?
options: Everything inside a free app is always free
The upgrade may charge money even though the app was free
pre.why: In-app purchases are separate transactions; check terms, controls and receipts.

pre.question: Two people edit a shared document together at the same time. What is this?
pre.why: Synchronous collaboration happens at the same time; asynchronous work happens at different times.

pre.question: A reviewer should suggest wording but not directly rewrite the file. Which access fits when supported?
pre.why: Commenter access fits feedback without granting direct editing rights.

pre.question: Which feedback is most useful?
options: Add a contact number after the steps so readers can find help.
pre.why: Useful feedback names a specific change and explains the benefit.

pre.question: Before recording a class video meeting, what should you do?
options: Assume joining is always recording consent
Ask permission and follow the group’s rules
pre.why: Meeting etiquette includes checking recording permissions and respecting participants.

pre.question: What is an example of universal design?
options: Controls usable by keyboard as well as mouse
pre.why: Universal design increases usability across needs and situations.

pre.question: An online contact uses a false identity to build trust. What is this commonly called?
pre.why: Catfishing uses a false identity to build trust or manipulate someone. Pause and verify independently.

pre.question: You find an unknown USB drive in the lab. What should you do?
options: Give it to authorized staff without plugging it in
Open it to find the owner
pre.why: Untrusted portable media can carry harmful software. Follow approved device procedures.

pre.question: What is the purpose of encryption?
options: Make data unreadable without the appropriate key
Reduce all files to half their size
pre.why: Encryption protects data readability. It does not replace other account, device or trust checks.

post.question: The text on a service website is too small. What should you try first?
post.why: Browser zoom changes webpage size. Choose the control that matches the problem.

post.question: A volunteer scheduler only needs to know when you are unavailable. What should you share?
post.why: Free/busy can support scheduling without disclosing event details. Verify the service’s options.

post.question: Autocomplete suggests the wrong email address. What is the best response?
options: Check and choose the intended address
Send it because the app suggested it
Share your password with both people
post.why: Automation can save time but needs review, especially for names, addresses and meaning.

post.question: A handout is going to a shared lab printer. What should you verify first?
options: Whether the email inbox is empty
Printer destination, preview and a test page
post.why: Verify the destination and output before sending a large print job.

post.question: Before posting in a professional group, what should you check?
options: Whether your personal posts are entertaining
The active identity, audience and account credentials
post.why: Check the identity and audience. Keep credentials distinct and use appropriate account protections.

post.question: You need feedback next week. What is a considerate communication choice?
options: State the deadline and respect expected working hours
Demand an immediate reply at any hour
Send the same message every five minutes
post.why: Timing and a clear response expectation help the recipient respond appropriately.

post.question: A new teammate does not know an abbreviation. What should you do?
options: Assume their age explains the problem
Explain it plainly without making assumptions
post.why: Inclusive communication explains context and avoids assumptions about age, culture or ability.

post.question: You cannot find a command in an updated app. What is the best next step?
options: Share your password in a public forum
Use current official help and describe the exact task
Download the first unfamiliar fix offered
post.why: Version-specific help and a precise question support independent learning.

post.question: You need local public-library opening hours. Which query best fits?
options: Library name, town and opening hours
post.why: Search terms should identify the service and location needed for the task.

post.question: A directory promises a local service without naming a source. What is the best check?
options: Assume a polished design proves the claim
Confirm availability through the provider’s official contact
post.why: Responsible sources and corroborating evidence matter more than ranking or appearance.

post.question: A reliable article explains an old program that no longer operates locally. What is the problem?
options: It may be outdated or irrelevant to this task
post.why: Accuracy, currency and relevance are separate questions.

post.question: A service-request form asks for information unrelated to the request. What should you do?
options: Check the purpose and collector before providing it
Fill every field with real private information
Assume all forms have the same rules
post.why: Understand the collection purpose, provide only needed information, and check the result.

post.question: How should you mark a document’s main sections?
options: Turn the entire document into an image
post.why: Real heading styles provide structure; visual bolding alone does not.

post.question: C2, C3 and C4 contain quantities. Which formula totals that range?
post.why: A colon marks an inclusive cell range. Verify the formula by changing one input.

post.question: You want to adapt someone else’s diagram. What is the right first step?
options: Check allowed uses and attribution conditions
Use it without credit if it is small
Assume a screenshot avoids all restrictions
post.why: Find the actual reuse permission and follow its conditions.

post.question: A coauthor must change wording in your handout. What should you provide?
options: The editable file with suitable permissions
post.why: Choose the format and access that support the recipient’s task. PDF is often useful for finished layout.

post.question: Which subject best helps a recipient act on a schedule question?
options: Please confirm the resource workshop start time
post.why: A specific subject tells the recipient what the message concerns.

post.question: You use Bcc for an announcement. What protection does it provide?
options: Conceals that recipient list from other recipients
Guarantees the message cannot be forwarded
post.why: Bcc hides recipient addresses; it does not encrypt content or prevent forwarding.

post.question: A streaming offer starts at no charge. What should you check before accepting?
options: Whether it renews, the price and how to cancel
post.why: Free trials can become recurring subscriptions. Review the terms and total cost.

post.question: A downloaded app offers extra features for purchase. What is a sensible step?
options: Share a payment password with the group
Review the charge and purchase controls before authorizing
Approve automatically because downloading was free
post.why: In-app purchases are separate transactions; check terms, controls and receipts.

post.question: A team coauthors a file during a live call. Which description fits?
post.why: Synchronous collaboration happens at the same time; asynchronous work happens at different times.

post.question: A partner only needs to leave feedback on your draft. Which permission is appropriate when available?
options: Unrestricted editing by anyone with the link
post.why: Commenter access fits feedback without granting direct editing rights.

post.question: Which comment best helps improve a shared handout?
options: Define this abbreviation so a new reader can follow the instructions.
post.why: Useful feedback names a specific change and explains the benefit.

post.question: You want to save a webinar discussion that includes participants. What should guide your decision?
options: Organizer rules and appropriate recording permission
Whether the record button is easy to find
Only how much storage you have
post.why: Meeting etiquette includes checking recording permissions and respecting participants.

post.question: Which feature helps people use technology in different situations?
post.why: Universal design increases usability across needs and situations.

post.question: Someone invents a personal profile to manipulate a relationship. Which term fits?
post.why: Catfishing uses a false identity to build trust or manipulate someone. Pause and verify independently.

post.question: A stranger offers a USB drive with a useful app. What is the safest class response?
options: Do not connect it; consult authorized support
post.why: Untrusted portable media can carry harmful software. Follow approved device procedures.

post.question: An encrypted device is lost while powered off. What does encryption help protect?
options: The truth of all messages ever received
The ability to cancel every subscription
The readability of stored data without its key
post.why: Encryption protects data readability. It does not replace other account, device or trust checks.
